title: Autonomous AI Agents & Tool-Calling Systems (PYTH_182_S1 to PYTH_182_S8)

slides.title: ReAct Framework & Agent Loops
slides.prompt: Autonomous agents combine Reasoning and Acting (ReAct) in iterative loops to evaluate goals, execute tool functions, and observe results.
slides.codeSnippet:
# ReAct Loop Pattern
while not done:
    thought = agent.plan(history)
    action = agent.decide_tool(thought)
    observation = execute_tool(action)
    history.append((thought, action, observation))

slides.title: Function Calling Schema Definitions
slides.prompt: How do LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) determine when and how an agent should invoke a Python tool?
options: Via structured JSON Schema definitions describing tool parameters, data types, and function descriptions
By reading Python docstrings directly from local source files at runtime
By executing raw shell commands inside isolated Docker environments
Through static C++ header file bindings
slides.correctAnswer: Via structured JSON Schema definitions describing tool parameters, data types, and function descriptions

slides.title: Stateful Agent Memory Persistence
slides.prompt: Which memory mechanism allows multi-turn autonomous agents to retain conversational state across user sessions?
options: Vector-backed or database-persisted message history queues
Writing temporary log files to standard error
Storing states in HTTP response cookies
slides.correctAnswer: Vector-backed or database-persisted message history queues

slides.title: Agent Execution Loop Infinite Loop Prevention
slides.prompt: How do agent runtimes prevent infinite loops when an agent fails to arrive at a final answer?
options: By enforcing a strict `max_iterations` cutoff limit on the execution loop
By automatically shutting down the cloud host machine
By converting tool output variables into null types
slides.correctAnswer: By enforcing a strict `max_iterations` cutoff limit on the execution loop
